title: node-forge RSA signature verification: Vision One applicability assessment
summary: Reviewed release manifests for Vision One 27.2.0, 27.2.1 and 27.2.2 include node-forge 1.4.0, which is covered by CVE-2026-85393. The affected verifier is reachable through local CSR handling. Remote exploitability in Vision One has not been established; the assessment remains open. High severity refers to the upstream library advisory, not a separately established Vision One product score.

affected.product: Vision One server / Windows Runtime (dependency inclusion confirmed from release manifests)
affected.versions: 27.2.0, 27.2.1 and 27.2.2 include node-forge 1.4.0. These are the reviewed releases, not a complete affected-version range. Earlier releases and prereleases have not been comprehensively assessed in this notice and must not be assumed unaffected.
affected.action: Review local certificate/CSR file permissions and administrative access, retain OT network segmentation, and monitor this advisory. Updating to 27.2.2 does not remove this dependency finding. Contact admin@energy-control.it for installation-specific assessment.

impact: CVE-2026-85393 concerns acceptance of extra elements in the nested DigestAlgorithm sequence during node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification. Upstream reports that this can permit signature forgery with low-public-exponent RSA keys. The GitHub-reviewed upstream rating is High, CVSS 4.0 8.7 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N). This is an upstream base score, not a Vision One-specific exploitability assessment. No Vision One-specific CVSS score is assigned by this notice, and no authentication, license or TLS bypass is claimed to have been demonstrated.
assessment: Scope and evidence: the server release lockfiles at tags 27.2.0, 27.2.1 and 27.2.2 each list node-forge 1.4.0 as a production dependency. The reviewed application CSR and certificate-policy code is unchanged between those tags. This assessment is based on source and dependency-manifest review plus a benign library test, not an independent penetration test or extraction and examination of every published installer.

node-forge is actively used for local RSA key, certificate and CSR generation, CSR verification, certificate metadata parsing and ASN.1 algorithm inspection. Both newly generated CSRs and an existing CSR read from the local certificate directory can reach node-forge's RSA verification code. A benign RSA-3072 CSR round-trip confirmed that csr.verify() calls the RSA public-key verifier; this establishes code-path reachability, not successful exploitation.

Default application-generated RSA keys use 3072-bit moduli and public exponent 65537. This does not establish that every existing or externally provisioned key has the same exponent, nor does it make the affected library fixed. The reviewed CSR inputs are generated by the application or read from its local certificate directory. No unauthenticated remote endpoint accepting arbitrary CSR verification input was identified in the reviewed paths.

The reviewed server dependency metadata and a literal-import scan of the installed server dependencies did not identify an additional third-party consumer of node-forge. This is a bounded static review, not proof that every possible dynamic path or customer integration has been assessed.

The reviewed HTTPS and Project Replication transport paths use Node.js TLS/crypto, with certificate identity and fingerprint checks where configured; their use of node-forge for parsing or algorithm inspection does not by itself route TLS signature verification through the affected RSA verifier. License signatures use Node.js crypto with Ed25519 rather than this node-forge RSA path. These observations are limited to this CVE and are not a general security guarantee.

Conclusion as of 2026-10-20: the vulnerable dependency is present and the affected verification function is reachable in local CSR handling. An exploitable remote Vision One path has not been established by this review. Product applicability remains under assessment; the finding is not classified as resolved or comprehensively mitigated. This initial publication will be revised if the affected scope, practical impact or remediation changes.
remediation: As of 2026-10-20, the GitHub-reviewed upstream advisory lists node-forge versions up to and including 1.4.0 as affected and lists no patched release. No fixed Vision One version is identified in this notice. The previously communicated replacement of the node-forge PKI implementation remains planned work, not a shipped remedy or a guaranteed delivery date. Do not install unofficial forks, replace packaged library files, or regard a general product update as a fix for this CVE without a corresponding revised advisory.
workarounds: Restrict write access to the Vision One runtime data root and certificate/CSR directory to trusted, necessary operating-system accounts. Treat accounts able to modify private keys, CSRs, certificates or runtime files as security-sensitive.

Accept externally provisioned certificate/key/CSR material only through approved, trusted PKI and maintenance procedures. Do not substitute untrusted files or relax existing certificate and peer-fingerprint checks.

Restrict administrative access and keep runtime and replication endpoints within approved OT segments, VPNs or equivalent site controls. Network segmentation is defense in depth, not a demonstrated complete workaround for this library vulnerability.

No workaround has been validated as fully eliminating this finding for all supported deployment configurations. Follow this advisory for updates and request installation-specific guidance if certificate/CSR provenance or permissions are uncertain.
